question: What is the primary role of the nurse regarding drug hazards?

options.A: Serving as the final safety barrier before administration
options.B: Manufacturing safer pharmaceutical compounds for hospital use
options.C: Determining the exact chemical composition of all prescribed drugs
options.D: Prescribing alternative medications to avoid dangerous side effects

explanation: Nurses check medications right before giving them to catch errors made earlier in the process. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h1)

question: Why must a nurse view pharmacotherapy as a balance between benefits and risks?

options.A: Therapeutic effects only occur when toxic reactions are actively triggered
options.B: Patients will refuse treatment if they know about any potential side effects
options.C: Every medication carries some level of inherent hazard alongside its healing properties
options.D: Hospital policies require reporting all minor medication side effects daily

explanation: All drugs have the potential to cause harm, so nurses must weigh therapeutic gains against possible toxic effects. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h1)

question: Which type of adverse drug reaction is predictable and related to the drug's normal pharmacological action?
explanation: Type A reactions are augmented pharmacological effects that happen because the drug is working too strongly. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h2)

question: A patient develops a sudden, severe allergic skin rash after taking a common antibiotic for the first time. How is this reaction classified?
explanation: Type B reactions are bizarre, unpredictable, and do not relate to the drug's normal pharmacological effects. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h2)

question: What is the main result of impaired drug excretion by the kidneys?

options.A: Rapid elimination of the drug through the skin
options.B: Drug accumulation and potential toxicity in the body
options.C: Immediate breakdown of the drug in the stomach
options.D: Increased therapeutic effectiveness with zero side effects

explanation: When kidneys cannot filter waste properly, drugs stay in the blood longer and build up to dangerous levels. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h3)

question: Why can a standard, correct dose of a medication still cause toxicity in certain individuals?

options.A: All standard doses are actually calculated to cause mild toxicity first
options.B: Slowed organ clearance can cause the drug to build up over time
options.C: Standard doses only work if the patient takes them with food
options.D: The liver automatically destroys standard doses before they work

explanation: If liver or kidney function is reduced, normal doses cannot be cleared fast enough, leading to toxic buildup. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h3)

question: Why are neonates especially vulnerable to drug toxicity?

options.A: Immature liver enzymes and undeveloped kidney filtration
options.B: An unusually high metabolic rate that burns up medications
options.C: A complete lack of blood circulation to internal organs
options.D: Increased total body fat that traps water-soluble drugs

explanation: Babies cannot break down and excrete drugs efficiently because their organs are still developing. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h4)

question: A patient with severe liver disease is prescribed a medication that is normally broken down by hepatic enzymes. What is the most appropriate nursing concern?

options.A: The liver disease will instantly cure itself once the pill is swallowed
options.B: The drug may build up in the body and cause toxic effects
options.C: The medication will pass through the body without any effect at all
options.D: The drug will be eliminated too quickly to provide any relief

explanation: A damaged liver cannot metabolize drugs effectively, leading to dangerous levels accumulating in the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary effect of grapefruit juice on certain medications?

options.A: Binding directly to the drug to prevent any absorption
options.B: Inhibiting intestinal enzymes and increasing drug blood levels
options.C: Speeding up kidney excretion to reduce drug effectiveness
options.D: Neutralizing the chemical pH of the drug in the stomach

explanation: Grapefruit juice blocks specific enzymes in the gut, allowing much more medication to enter the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h5)

question: What happens when a patient takes two different medications that both depress the central nervous system?

options.A: Liver enzymes shut down permanently to prevent any chemical processing
options.B: An additive or synergistic sedative effect that can impair breathing
options.C: The two drugs cancel each other out completely with no effect
options.D: The patient experiences a sudden burst of high physical energy

explanation: Combining multiple depressants multiplies their calming effects on the brain and can dangerously slow breathing. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h5)

question: Which action must a nurse take BEFORE giving a high-risk medication?

options.A: Ask the patient to sign a waiver releasing the hospital from liability
options.B: Gather baseline clinical data and relevant lab values
options.C: Discontinue all other medications the patient is currently taking
options.D: Double the prescribed dose to test for allergic reactions

explanation: Baseline checks give you a reference point to compare against if the patient develops adverse symptoms later. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h6)

question: A patient taking a new blood pressure medication suddenly feels very dizzy and lightheaded when standing up. What is the most appropriate immediate nursing action?

options.A: Tell the patient to run in place to improve blood circulation
options.B: Administer a stimulant medication to raise the blood pressure
options.C: Check the patient's blood pressure and pulse immediately
options.D: Wait until the next scheduled clinic visit to report the finding

explanation: Dizziness after starting a new blood pressure drug points to orthostatic hypotension, requiring a check of vital signs. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h6)

question: What is the very first action a nurse should take when a patient shows signs of severe drug toxicity?

options.A: Stop the administration of the offending medication
options.B: Increase the intravenous fluid rate without a doctor's order
options.C: Document the event in the patient's chart at the end of the shift
options.D: Ask the patient to walk around the room to stay awake

explanation: Stopping the drug source prevents any more of the toxic substance from entering the patient's system. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h7)

question: Why are intravenous fluids often ordered for a patient experiencing drug toxicity?

options.A: To instantly neutralize the chemical pH of all oral medications
options.B: To help flush water-soluble drugs out through the kidneys
options.C: To dilute the remaining blood cells in the circulatory system
options.D: To replace liver tissue damaged by the toxic substance

explanation: Hydration supports kidney output, helping the body eliminate circulating toxins faster through urine. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h7)

question: What is the main goal of pharmacovigilance in healthcare?

options.A: Marketing new pharmaceutical products to regional hospitals
options.B: Detecting, assessing, and preventing adverse drug effects
options.C: Speeding up the clinical drug trial approval process
options.D: Calculating the financial cost of manufactured medications

explanation: Pharmacovigilance is the ongoing safety monitoring process designed to catch and prevent drug-related harm. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h8)

question: Why is it important to report medication near-misses and errors through institutional incident reporting systems?

options.A: It helps the healthcare team identify systemic flaws to prevent future harm
options.B: It allows the pharmacy to bill the insurance company for wasted drugs
options.C: It ensures that negligent nurses are immediately fired from the facility
options.D: It provides legal protection for the hospital during malpractice lawsuits

explanation: Reporting errors highlights weak spots in the medication system so safety procedures can be improved. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h8)
